thread:
olivia: Heads-up — ACME Ops hit us about their trial credits running out mid-loadtest. They say they were ramping traffic and dropped into 429s when credits expired. Asking for a short grace window or manual credit top-up.
ryan: Account ID? any unusual usage patterns?
olivia: acct: acme-prod-42, customer claims they were on a pre-sale demo with a partner and traffic spike was intentional. I pulled recent usage: heavy burst over a 3h window, token usage ~3.2M. Promo applied earlier: TRIAL2025 for $200 credit.
sophia: Can you paste the promo application log? sometimes promo gets applied but an overlapping billing flag blocks it.
olivia: Sure — from billing-bot logs: `promo_apply: TRIAL2025 success -> balance +200.00; auto-expire: 2026-03-12T23:59:59Z; usage_deducted -> 3.2M tokens; balance_zero at 2026-03-14T09:12:11Z`
ryan: So it expired on the 12th UTC and they hit zero on the 14th after sustained use. Looks like they continued load beyond expiration.
sophia: Policy: trial credits are time-limited and we generally don't extend unless there's a clear platform-side failure. Did they report any API errors or auth failures that prevented them from throttling?
olivia: They mention 'rate limit errors' once credits drained. No reports of unexpected 5xx or auth issues. Customer says they weren't notified until the last minute.
ryan: We send expiry email 48h before and a final notice at 4h. Did the outbound-email logs show delivery?
uff — billing-bot: "email_event: account acme-prod-42, expiry_notice_48h -> delivered; expiry_notice_4h -> delivered"
sophia: That suggests notifications were sent. Still, for goodwill we can offer a one-time discretionary promo of $100 and recommend they stagger load tests or bump to Dedicated for predictable throughput.
eng-oncall: Quick note — if the customer's test created abnormal burst shaping on the serving side we should review for any throttling or throttling traces, but nothing in SLOs flagged.
ryan: OK. Two asks: 1) Olivia please confirm customer accepts a $100 manual grant and send the exact wording. 2) Can finance sign-off on one-time manual promo? tagging @finance (I can loop them if you want).
olivia: Draft reply for customer: "Sorry about the interruption — we confirmed your trial credit expired on 2026-03-12. As a one-time courtesy we've added a $100 manual credit to your account to finish the test. Please let us know if you'd like help scheduling a follow-up run or exploring Dedicated capacity." Thoughts?
sophia: Clean. Add a note about promo expiry (30 days) and that it's not a recurring grant. Also include how to avoid this: enable rate-limiting in client or contact us before big tests.
olivia: Updated message sent. Waiting on finance approval.
ryan: Finance approved via email thread — go ahead.
olivia: Done, billing-bot shows `manual_credit: +100.00 -> reason: discretionary goodwill; expires: 2026-04-15`. Customer replied :thumbsup: "Thanks, that'll work — please also share best practices for loadtests."
sophia: Can we add a KB link for load test runbook and a short template for next time? I'll draft and ping ops to add to onboarding.
ryan: Great. Closing loop: no policy exception needed beyond CS discretionary; documented in account notes.
olivia: Marking thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
